n1.speaker: tendai
n1.text: Three cars at the gate this morning, {player}. Three! People who drove two hours to look at our animals.

n2.speaker: tendai
n2.text: Visitors pay at the gate. Ten a head. More if they can actually see something.

n3.speaker: amara
n3.text: More people means more noise and more cars. Animals notice. Let them come, but give them somewhere to watch from.

n4.speaker: tendai
n4.text: An observation tower, then. Up on the plains, where the herds cross. Ruth always wanted one.

n5.speaker: narrator
n5.text: Build an observation tower (Build, B). Visitors come for the animals: the more species you have, and the better your reputation, the more come.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: A family stands at the foot of the tower, passing a pair of binoculars back and forth.

n1.speaker: tendai
n1.text: The little one saw the lions. She has not stopped talking since.

n2.speaker: amara
n2.text: Every visitor who goes home happy tells ten more. Every one who sees nothing tells twenty.

n3.speaker: amara
n3.text: The more different animals they can see, the better. Giraffe would help. And if the old stories about a leopard on the rocks are true…

start.speaker: amara
start.text: I have been on the phone to a reserve up north. They have giraffe and wildebeest to spare, if we can pay for the move.

n1.speaker: amara
n1.text: Giraffe browse the trees that nothing else reaches. Wildebeest share the grass with the zebras. Both would bring visitors.

n2.speaker: tendai
n2.text: And both need a vet to travel. Hire one if we have not got one yet.

n3.speaker: narrator
n3.text: Bring species in from the Species menu (K). It needs a vet and money; the reserve needs 8 species to count as whole again.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: A long silver car pulls up at the gate. The man who steps out is smiling before his shoes touch the dust.

n1.speaker: victor
n1.text: Victor Hale. We have written to each other. Well, I wrote. You must be very busy.

n2.speaker: victor
n2.text: Your tower is charming. Your visitors are charming. But they drive home at night, and their money drives with them.

n3.speaker: victor
n3.text: Let me build you a lodge. Free of charge. Twenty beds, a deck over the plains. In return, Hale & Partners takes a modest share of the ticket money.

choices.text: Thank you, but we will build our own, in our own time.
Before we talk business: what do you know about the old pump?

accept.speaker: victor
accept.text: Wonderful. My builders start tomorrow. You will not regret it.

n7.speaker: tendai
n7.text: Ruth sent him away three times. I hope you know what you are doing.

decline.speaker: victor
decline.text: Of course. Independence. Admirable. The offer stays open, as long as the reserve does.

pump.speaker: victor
pump.text: The pump? I have no idea what you mean. I build lodges, not plumbing.

n10.speaker: narrator
n10.text: For a moment the smile is gone. Then it is back, a little thinner.

n11.speaker: victor
n11.text: Think about my offer. Things out here break so easily. It would be a shame.

end.speaker: narrator
end.text: The silver car leaves a long cloud of dust on the east road.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: The rocky outcrop rises out of the northern plains, warm and quiet.

n1.speaker: tendai
n1.text: Leopard country. When I was young there was a female up here. I saw her twice in ten years.

n2.speaker: tendai
n2.text: Look at this. Fresh tracks, and a kill dragged up into that fig. She has a daughter, or I am a zebra.

n3.speaker: tendai
n3.text: They come down to the plains at dusk to hunt impala. Keep your eyes on the northern edge of the plains. If you spot her, the visitors will hear about it.

start.speaker: amara
start.text: A leopard! On camera, in daylight. Do you know how rare that is?

n1.speaker: tendai
n1.text: Ruth would have framed that photo and hung it in the office.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: At dusk two rangers walk a young man in to the office. His hands are scratched and his shoes are worn through.

n1.speaker: tendai
n1.text: Caught him near the rocks with a coil of wire and a bag of snares.

n2.speaker: kito
n2.text: I did not set them. I only carry them. A man pays me to carry them. Two hundred for a bag.

n3.speaker: kito
n3.text: My name is Kito. My mother is sick. Two hundred is a month of medicine.

choices.text: Tendai, talk to him. Find out who pays him.

police.speaker: narrator
police.text: The police van takes Kito away before midnight. He does not look back.

talk.speaker: tendai
talk.text: Sit, boy. Drink this. Now. From the beginning, and slowly.

n7.speaker: kito
n7.text: I only ever see the driver. A big truck, no lights. It comes in from the east road when there is no moon.

end.speaker: tendai
end.text: Snares near the rocks, where the leopards hunt. Somebody knows what lives here.

n9.speaker: tendai
n9.text: One more thing. A ranger saw strange tracks by the north fence last week. Go and look before the rain takes them.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: In the mud by the north fence there is a footprint as wide as a dinner plate, with three toes.

n1.speaker: amara
n1.text: That is a rhino. A big one. No question.

n2.speaker: tendai
n2.text: There has not been a rhino here since before Ruth died. If one has walked in from the north…

choices.text: Then we protect it, whatever it takes.
Keep this quiet. Nobody outside hears about it.

protect.speaker: tendai
protect.text: Whatever it takes may be a lot.

quiet.speaker: amara
quiet.text: Agreed. A rhino is worth more to a poacher than this whole reserve is to a bank.

end.speaker: narrator
end.text: You photograph the print and send the rangers home by the long way.

start.speaker: tendai
start.text: The visitors keep asking where they can watch from. An observation tower on the plains would do it (Build, B).

start.speaker: amara
start.text: Visitors want variety. Giraffe or wildebeest from the north, and our leopards if we can find them. The Species menu (K) has the transfer offers.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: A season of visitors. A tower full of binoculars, eight kinds of animal on the plains, and one footprint in the mud.

n1.speaker: amara
n1.text: The reserve pays for itself now, nearly. I did not think I would see that.

n2.speaker: tendai
n2.text: Money brings people. People bring eyes. Some of those eyes are looking at our rhino.

lodge.speaker: tendai
lodge.text: And Hale’s lodge sits on our plains, full of Hale’s staff, watching everything.

cold.speaker: tendai
cold.text: And Hale has not written since you asked him about the pump. Not one letter. That worries me more than his letters did.

plain.speaker: tendai
plain.text: And Hale still sends a letter every week, each one a little less polite.

end.speaker: tendai
end.text: If there is a rhino out there, {player}, someone else knows it too.
